reason: Driven at 1440x960 and 390x844 from both entry points (owner-flight Add, and owner-empty -> set the day -> Add). Harvest: row title "Untitled moment"; grab aria-label "Edit Untitled moment. Saturday 25 July, in 9 days. Shown to guests."; panel aria-label "Editing Untitled moment"; field value "" (length 0) with placeholder "What is happening"; label "What it is"; document.activeElement === b-edit-title. So the field is EMPTY with a placeholder, not pre-filled - the finding's own premise reduces to one transient row title. (1) The count of three is wrong. "Untitled moment" is a name, "What it is" is a field-name chip (b.css:720 - mono, size-label, uppercase, fore-62), "What is happening" is an in-field prompt. Three classes of string, not three names. The behaviour gate at interaction-check.mjs:1478-1487 ("an untitled moment is named once") already proves the name is ONE name across row, accessible name and panel; the finding restates that assertion and then miscounts against it. (2) The register claim is overstated by the interaction. The moment is created with the editor already open and focus already in the title field (render-b.js:1339-1342 and openEditor), and setTitle repaints the row on every input event - typed "H" and the row became "H" and the panel "Editing H" within 200ms. The string the finding calls the impressionable owner's first impression survives exactly one keystroke, under a blinking cursor. (3) The fix makes it worse where it touches most. "Not named yet" is a predicate phrase forced into name slots: "Editing Not named yet", "Edit Not named yet. Saturday 25 July, in 9 days." (a screen reader hears an ungrammatical run-on), and worst, the rename receipt at render-b.js:809 becomes "Renamed to Not named yet." - a sentence asserting an action that did not happen. Round 7 established one name usable in every slot (render-b.js:43-49); a predicate phrase cannot fill a name slot, so the fix breaks the invariant it is standing on. (4) "Set in the same ink as the placeholder" collides with a ratified encoding: fore-62 title ink at weight 400 is already how a row hidden from guests is drawn (b.css:327-330). The newest moment, focused and being edited, would render in the exact ink that means hidden. (5) Deleting the placeholder removes the only sentence-grammar prompt inside the one field the owner is auto-focused into, leaving a bare box under a small uppercase mono chip. At best a wash; the empty-date field's hint (render-b.js:1314-1316) shows this build already moved persistent information OUT of placeholders and kept prompts in them - a considered position, not an oversight. Net: a rename plus gate churn in three assertions, buying a worse receipt, a worse accessible name and a title ink that lies about visibility.
